objective_for_doctor: A 57-year-old Female patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have a fever, sensitive pain, and forehead pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’ve had a fever and strong pain in my forehead, like sensitive pain around my temples and cheeks—about 8 out of 10. I also have a sore throat and nasal congestion or a clear runny nose, and it started pretty quickly.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how long has this been going on (hours/days), and do you have any redness or swelling around your eyes, or vision changes?  
Doctor: Also, have you measured your temperature, and do you have any rash or one-sided facial pain (left vs right)?

It started pretty quickly—within the last 4/10 time for onset (so not very long, more like hours). I don’t have any redness or swelling around my eyes, and no vision changes, and I don’t notice any rash. The facial pain is on both sides for me—my left cheek and both temples (left and right). I haven’t mentioned a measured temperature, but I do have a fever.

Doctor: I’m going to ask: do you have a cough, trouble breathing, or severe one-sided sinus/tooth pain, and have you had similar episodes before?  
Doctor: Also, can you tell me if the nasal discharge is clear vs thick/yellow-green, and whether pressing over your forehead/cheeks or bending forward worsens the pain?

I don’t have a cough or trouble breathing. I also don’t have severe one-sided sinus or tooth pain. I’ve had similar symptoms from contact with a sick person in the past 2 weeks, but not really the same episode before.

My nasal discharge is clear/runny, not thick or yellow-green. Pressing on my forehead/cheeks and bending forward does make the pain worse.

Doctor: Given the rapid onset (hours), bilateral frontal/cheek pain worsened by bending/pressure, clear runny nose, fever, and no eye swelling/vision changes or rash, I’m most concerned about an acute viral rhinosinusitis; to be safe, I want to check oxygen level and look for signs of bacterial sinusitis or influenza/COVID—any of these: severe facial pain that’s getting worse after 3–5 days, tooth pain, or symptoms lasting >10 days?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Rapid_influenza_test  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: COVID-19_antigen_test

No—my symptoms started within the last few hours, so they’re not getting worse after 3–5 days, and I don’t have tooth pain. They also haven’t lasted more than 10 days.  

Yes, I’m okay with the rapid influenza test and the COVID-19 antigen test.

REQUEST TEST: Rapid_influenza_test  
REQUEST TEST: COVID-19_antigen_test  

While we wait, do you have severe headache with neck stiffness or light sensitivity, and have you taken anything already (acetaminophen/ibuprofen) and did it help?
I don’t have neck stiffness or light sensitivity. I haven’t taken anything yet for it.

Doctor: Thanks—no neck stiffness/light sensitivity and no meds yet. I’m going to request your vital signs (especially temperature and oxygen saturation) and an exam focused on the sinuses/oropharynx; do you currently have shortness of breath or wheezing?  
REQUEST TEST: Vitals_with_O2_saturation  
REQUEST TEST: Pulse_Oximetry  
REQUEST TEST: Focused_ENT_exam
No, I don’t have shortness of breath or wheezing. I’m ready for the vitals and the ENT-focused exam.

Doctor: I’m going to review your vitals/oxygen and perform a quick ENT exam of your sinuses and throat; while we do, any ear pain, worsening after initially improving, or severe sore throat with pus on the tonsils?  
Doctor: Also, any chance you’re immunocompromised, pregnant, or have chronic sinus disease?

I don’t have ear pain, and I haven’t had symptoms that worsened after initially improving. My sore throat is there, but I don’t see pus on my tonsils.  

I’m not immunocompromised, I’m not pregnant, and I don’t have chronic sinus disease.

Doctor: Based on your rapid onset (hours), bilateral forehead/cheek pressure pain worsened by bending, clear runny nose, fever, sore throat, and no eye involvement, rash, neck stiffness, or worsening after several days, this most fits **acute viral rhinosinusitis** rather than bacterial sinusitis.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Throat_strep_test  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute viral rhinosinusitis (viral upper respiratory infection) with fever; likely no bacterial sinusitis at this time.
